strategy.summary: Reproduce GH#66510 in pandas at buggy commit 982854070758: a datetime that renders or shifts onto iNaT (INT64_MIN) is silently returned as NaT instead of raising OutOfBoundsDatetime. Build pandas from source, then run the developer's Timestamp constructor tests that expect that rejection. The numerical_failure text describes a different defect (timedelta64 nansum in float64, issue 66551), so the developer tests are the grading target, not that text.

system_packages: a C/C++ compiler toolchain (gcc or clang) for the Cython/C extensions
pinned_because: No pin applied. NumPy, python-dateutil, tzdata and Cython are all unbounded in the evidence (no documented constraint, no era ceiling), so current releases compatible with the checked-out revision are chosen.
meson-python, meson and ninja are added because --no-build-isolation requires the build backend preinstalled; they are inferred from pandas' build system, not from the evidence.

strategy.reproducing_test: pandas/tests/scalar/timestamp/test_constructors.py::test_constructor_naive_datetime_renders_nat_sentinel together with test_constructor_datetime64_tz_shift_hits_nat_sentinel, test_constructor_aware_datetime_offset_hits_nat_sentinel, test_constructor_str_shift_hits_nat_sentinel, test_constructor_aware_datetime_offset_overflow and test_constructor_offset_shifts_off_nat_sentinel (the last one is a must-pass guard), plus the io parser tests in pandas/tests/io/parser/test_parse_dates.py and the to_datetime tests in pandas/tests/tools/test_to_datetime.py for wider coverage.
strategy.success_criterion: On the buggy revision 982854070758, test_constructor_naive_datetime_renders_nat_sentinel fails: Timestamp(datetime(1677,9,21,0,12,43,145224), nanosecond=192) does not raise, so pytest.raises reports DID NOT RAISE. On the fixed revision the same test passes because OutOfBoundsDatetime is raised with message 'Out of bounds nanosecond timestamp: 1677-09-21 00:12:43.145224192'. The transition is buggy FAIL to fixed PASS for the selected -k nat_sentinel set, while test_constructor_offset_shifts_off_nat_sentinel and test_constructor_nat_sentinel_neighbours pass on both revisions.
strategy.numerical_probe: Timestamp(datetime(1677,9,21,0,12,43,145224), nanosecond=192)._value should be -(2**63) if it is wrongly accepted, and the fixed code must raise instead; check the ._value integer directly, not a float64 comparison.

input_output_examples.buggy_output: Timestamp returned that reads back as NaT (no OutOfBoundsDatetime raised)
input_output_examples.expected_output: OutOfBoundsDatetime: Out of bounds nanosecond timestamp: 1677-09-21 00:12:43.145224192

risks: Scope mismatch: the numerical_failure evidence (Series timedelta64 sum in nansum, Timedelta.min sum returns NaT) is not exercised by the developer's test diff, which covers GH#66510 datetime iNaT rendering. Do not treat a timedelta sum reproduction as confirming this PR.

Platform: the sentinel is INT64_MIN and the arithmetic is platform independent on 64-bit Linux. The developer test does not state an architecture; no 32-bit or sanitiser requirement is evidenced, so none is assumed. A non-64-bit platform would not reproduce the int64 wrap.
Named-timezone leg: the to_datetime test with Etc/GMT-1 needs the tzdata package and zoneinfo data to be present, which is not confirmed by the evidence beyond tzdata being documented.

Memory-dependent behaviour: the evidence notes reads of info.deltas[ntrans] can differ between calls in one process, so tz-transition-based expectations may be flaky if the buggy path reads uninitialised memory. A repeated run is advisable before concluding.

Documented residual: the named-timezone strptime leg keeps a documented residual where a sentinel-rendering wall time still reads as NaT, so the to_datetime named-tz test may not transition cleanly; the constructor test is the primary target.

The test_command selects only the constructor file; the io parser (test_parse_dates.py, requires the C engine via low_memory) and to_datetime tests are not covered by it and need separate invocations.

Version choice: Python version, NumPy, dateutil, tzdata and Cython are all unbounded in the evidence, so the chosen versions are a judgement and may differ from those used when the defect was observed.

oracle.why: The developer tests compare integer ._value and raise-or-not outcomes exactly, so no tolerance is involved.

strategy.fails_on_buggy: On buggy revision 982854070758 the constructor does not raise, so pytest.raises fails with DID NOT RAISE (inferred from the described behaviour that a sentinel-rendering value is silently accepted and reads back as NaT).
strategy.passes_on_fixed: On the fixed revision OutOfBoundsDatetime is raised with the expected message, so the -k nat_sentinel constructor tests pass.
